title: CLAUDE.md — slurmworkflow
text: Workflow — named directory (workflows/<name>/) containing scripts metadata run sequence Slurm jobs HPC. Step — single sbatch submission within workflow. Steps run sequentially default via controller job chains . Step template — function factory defines step . package exports 7 templates: step_tmpl_bash_lines, step_tmpl_bash_script, step_tmpl_rscript, step_tmpl_do_call, step_tmpl_do_call_script, step_tmpl_map, step_tmpl_map_script. Workflow summary — -memory list (serialized workflow.yaml) tracks steps, sbatch options, workflow root path.

title: Build workflows for the Slurm workload manager
text: workflow sequence steps, step sbatch job submission. hood, slurmworkflow uses Slurm’s --dependency=afterany mechanism chain steps lightweight controller script: step can also alter execution flow runtime — enabling loops, conditional branching, dynamic multi-batch array job submission.
code: start_workflow.sh     └─▶ controller.sh (step 1)             └─▶ step 1 runs                     └─▶ controller.sh (step 2)                             └─▶ step 2 runs                                     └─▶ ...continues until all steps complete

title: Build workflows for the Slurm workload manager
text: Pass valid sbatch long-form option named list. Options set create_workflow() apply steps default; per-step options add_workflow_step() override . Mutually exclusive options (e.g., mem vs. mem-per-cpu vs. mem-per-gpu) validated automatically. partition option required.

title: Build workflows for the Slurm workload manager
text: Many HPC clusters limit maximum Slurm array size (commonly 1,000). step_tmpl_map() step_tmpl_map_script() accept max_array_size argument automatically chunks large arrays sequential batches: slurmworkflow handles batch sequencing internally — one batch array jobs completes, next batch automatically submitted.
code: # 10,000 scenarios, submitted in batches of 500 step_tmpl_map_script(   r_script = "R/run_sim.R",   scenario_id = 1:10000,   max_array_size = 500,   setup_lines = c("module load R/4.3.0") )

title: Build workflows for the Slurm workload manager
text: EpiModelHIV-Template repo demonstrates slurmworkflow used production HIV research projects. major analysis phase workflow-*.R file. representative workflow running intervention scenarios end--end: make_em_workflow() helper (defined template project) wraps create_workflow() project defaults always adds EpiModelHPC::step_tmpl_renv_restore() first step. pattern supports two levels parallelization: Slurm array jobs distribute scenarios across nodes, node runs ~32 simulations parallel internally. Typical workflow pipelines EpiModelHIV projects:
code: # R/F-intervention_scenarios/workflow-intervention.R (simplified) library(slurmworkflow) library(EpiModelHPC)  source("R/shared_variables.R") source("R/hpc_configs.R")  # Step 1: Create workflow + automatic renv restore step wf <- make_em_workflow("intervention")  # Step 2: Run intervention scenarios as a massive Slurm array job wf <- add_workflow_step(   wf_summary = wf,   step_tmpl = step_tmpl_netsim_scenarios(     path_to_est, param, init, control,     scenarios_list = scenarios_list,     output_dir = scenarios_dir,     n_rep = 32,     n_cores = max_cores,     max_array_size = 500,     setup_lines = hpc_node_setup   ),   sbatch_opts = list(     "cpus-per-task" = max_cores,     "time" = "04:00:00",     "mem-per-cpu" = "5G"   ) )  # Step 3: Merge distributed results into tidy tibbles wf <- add_workflow_step(   wf_summary = wf,   step_tmpl = step_tmpl_merge_netsim_scenarios_tibble(     sim_dir = scenarios_dir,     output_dir = merged_dir,     steps_to_keep = Inf,     setup_lines = hpc_node_setup   ),   sbatch_opts = list("mem" = "0", "time" = "04:00:00") )  # Step 4: Generate result tables wf <- add_workflow_step(   wf_summary = wf,   step_tmpl = step_tmpl_do_call_script(     r_script = "R/F-intervention_scenarios/4-tables.R",     args = list(hpc_context = TRUE),     setup_lines = hpc_node_setup   ),   sbatch_opts = list("mem" = "16G", "time" = "01:00:00") )  # Step 5: Generate plots wf <- add_workflow_step(   wf_summary = wf,   step_tmpl = step_tmpl_do_call_script(     r_script = "R/F-intervention_scenarios/5-plots.R",     args = list(hpc_context = TRUE),     setup_lines = hpc_node_setup   ),   sbatch_opts = list("mem" = "16G", "time" = "01:00:00") )
